title: introduce-playbook-fuzzer-sandbox-and-safe-dryrun-cli
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Run user authored runbooks/playbooks against synthesized incident signals to catch unsafe or flaky remediation steps before they reach oncall. This PR adds a sandboxed playbook fuzzer and a safe dry-run CLI (ibctl fuzz) to iterate locally and in CI.
Summary: 1) sandbox runtime that executes playbook actions in a constrained environment with side-effect emulation and explicit safety policies; 2) synthetic telemetry generator that produces a variety of incident footprints (latency spike, partial failure, cascading errors); 3) a deterministic fuzz harness that pairs telemetry traces with permutations of runbook steps; 4) ibctl CLI commands for local dry-run, CI batching, and exporting sanitized evidence snapshots for reviewers; 5) CI pipeline job that runs a daily regression matrix of approved playbooks.
Features & safety gates:
- Action policy whitelist with explicit opt-ins for any step that can mutate infra (e.g., restart services, run scripts).
- Timeboxed execution and quota limits for each playbook run.
- Safe-mode emulation where calls to external systems are stubbed and recorded.
- Automatic annotation of any step that would have performed a destructive action; those runs are marked as "requires human review" and fail CI unless explicitly allowed.
- Replayable sanitized snapshot exporter for human debugging.
How to use:
- Local: ibctl fuzz run --playbook path/to/playbook.yaml --seed 42 --mode dry-run
- Export evidence: ibctl fuzz export --run-id <id> --format json
- CI: .ci/fuzzer-pipeline.yml defines matrix entries; daily job posts results to #oncall-simulations.
Tests & validation:
- Unit tests for sandbox policies and fuzzer deterministic behavior.
- E2E test harness that runs certified sample playbooks under the sandbox and asserts no destructive side effects.
- Added a small corpus of canonical synthetic traces to catch regressions in runbook parsing.
Rollout plan:
- Feature flagged under experimental.fuzzer.
- Enable nightly CI runs for all repositories that include runbooks.
- We will monitor the fuzzer job for false positives for two weeks and adjust policy whitelist.
Checklist:
- [x] Implement sandbox runtime and policy engine
- [x] CLI and local runner
- [x] CI pipeline & secrets gating
- [x] Tests and sample corpus
- [x] Docs and runbook author guide (docs/playbook-fuzzer.md)
Related: ENG-1254 (fuzzer core), SRE-087 (oncall safety policy).

review_comments: Arjun Rao: This looks promising. Two questions: (1) how do we prevent accidental enabling of destructive opt-ins in CI? (answer please include gating at repo and org level), (2) any perf concerns for running the nightly matrix?

Maya Chen: Re: gating - opt-ins are stored in a per-repo allowlist file (runbooks/allowlist.yaml) and CI reads an org-level boolean to allow destructive runs; by default org boolean is off. Nightly matrix is intentionally sampled; we use deterministic seeding and an adjustable cap (default 50 runs) to limit cost.
Sasha Varga: Can you add an audit event for sandboxed-run results so Console can link the evidence snapshots to routes? Also add a tiny retention TTL config in the exporter.
Maya Chen: Added audit events (pkg/audit) and exporter TTL flag; documented in docs/playbook-fuzzer.md. PTAL.
Priya Nair: I ran the e2e locally; found a flaky timing assertion in playbook_fuzzer_test when the sandbox sleeps are too short. Recommend increasing wallclock tolerance or using a time mock.
Maya Chen: Switched to a controllable clock in the sandbox and removed flaky sleep; reran CI.
Arjun Rao: Approve after the timeout fix and CI green.
